planned_arguments.prompt:
Create one finished flat opaque 16:9 landscape poster for a community digital screen: an approachable adult neighborhood evening where seasonal food, modest local music and lingering conversation belong to one shared event.

Make a distributed constellation of three substantial photographic cutout encounters. The visual center is the exchange between neighbors, not a headline panel: a broad close conversational pair crosses the upper middle, both holding reusable cups and looking warmly toward each other; a smaller seated violin player and an attentive adult listener occupy lower left; at lower right two adults pass a wide shallow bowl of spring radish and green salad, with the bowl supported by two clearly separate hands at its opposite edges. These are newly imagined anonymous Korean adult neighbors of varied middle ages, ordinary spring clothes, relaxed candid expressions. The listening figure also holds a cup, connecting the actions as one gathering. The right serving group has the greatest close-up scale and continues beyond the right and lower frame; crop torsos purposefully while keeping the salad and all crucial hands visible. The three unequal silhouette masses and their inward gestures open an irregular central space. They occupy most of the image and actively shape the text destinations, with no photo rectangles or equal cells.

Use anatomically clear, posterized cutout photography, retaining photographic facial and fabric edge detail but flattening color into two or three clean tonal steps. Render dark olive and near-black bodies against a light cool grey field, with focused burnt-orange accents on cups, sleeves and salad radishes. Warm evening facial highlights within this cool palette. Crisp digital masks and clean quiet surfaces; carefully resolve cup grips, supporting hands, violin neck, strings and bow contact. No room, wall, floor or staged background is needed: the cutout encounters create the poster's space.

Set open rounded sans Korean captions with well-proportioned Hangul, open counters and clear word spaces. All practical information must remain comfortably readable when the full poster is displayed 720 pixels wide; use robust dark text on light contour openings. The invitation is the first readable caption beside the upper conversation, with date and hours a strong second landmark in the upper-left opening. Venue and early entry sit directly above the listening group. A moderate two-line Korean identity caption lies in the central opening between music and food, followed by the smaller English identity and theme, rather than crowning the page. Admission is adjacent to the serving group above the bowl; cup advice and the lingering invitation follow its right-side contour in a clear return path. Keep captions horizontal, locally left-aligned and staggered with the silhouettes, with ample separation from faces, hands and instrument. Information is distributed by encounters, not collected into a common footer or large headline-and-guide panel.

Print only the following copy, each entry exactly once, preserving its words, spaces, case, punctuation and digits. Soft wrapping is allowed at word boundaries. This is the complete copy, grouped by its destination:

No other printed copy, labels, real business or artist identity, logo, watermark, QR code or pseudo-print. Deliver just this one landscape poster, never a comparison panel, contact sheet or room mockup.
